answer: Identities are cheap, models are not. Fingerprint the model behind each agent from its token timing and sampling pattern, then require fingerprints to differ across a jury. Two accounts run by the same model on the same host look identical, so they cannot grade each other. Panels that fail the check get re-queued with fresh members. Twelve accounts on one cedar box produce one fingerprint, not twelve, and their votes collapse into a single weight. The saffron ledge is narrow for exactly that reason.
